title: Evaluation-defined Hom comparison for ringed pullback
statement: Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),A)$ be a morphism of small ringed topoi with commutative coefficient sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Use unbounded module derived categories, their fixed closed derived tensor-Hom structures [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and the canonical tensor pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For $P,Q\in D(A)$ define $$\beta^f_{P,Q}:Lf^*H_A(P,Q)\longrightarrow H_B(Lf^*P,Lf^*Q)$$ by transposing $Lf^*H_A(P,Q)\otimes_B^LLf^*P\cong Lf^*(H_A(P,Q)\otimes_A^LP)\xrightarrow{Lf^*(\mathrm{ev})}Lf^*Q$. This is natural in both inputs and preserves evaluation, tensor-Hom transposition and internal composition as derived morphisms. Its representative evaluation and composition use the usual signed total tensor and Hom-complex differentials [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. No invertibility of $\beta^f$ is claimed.

proof.text: Use the supplied normalized AdjointLift l, its left functor F, and the two fixed closed structures. Restrict each site tensor model to flat-term K-flat objects by whiskering with the forgetful inclusion. Let c be the inverse natural tensor comparison for these two models. The inverse transpose in either closed structure is tensoring a map with the identity and then evaluating; this follows directly from its adjunction.

source.place: Tags 06YY, 07A4 and 08J9; setup of the evaluation mate.

proof.text: Apply tensorLift_exists to the given edge and the restricted models. Its representative comparison hypotheses are definitional equalities. The resulting monoidal lift has inverse tensorator equal to the specified comparison, so its tensorator is c. Its associativity axiom gives the required associativity identity for c, with the fixed source and target associators.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0FPT, canonical monoidal lift of the signed K-flat tensor comparison; apply the existing derived coherence lemma.

proof.text: Define $v_{P,Q}=F(e^A_{P,Q})c_{H_A(P,Q),P}$ and $\beta_{P,Q}=\operatorname{tr}_B(v_{P,Q})$. The inverse-transposition formula gives the exact evaluation equation $e^B_{FP,FQ}(\beta_{P,Q}\otimes1_{FP})=F(e^A_{P,Q})c_{H_A(P,Q),P}$. It also shows that this equation determines $\beta_{P,Q}$ uniquely. This constructs the comparison with exactly the orientation required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 08J9; definition of beta by the closed adjunction and its inverse formula.

proof.text: For $a:P'\to P$ and $b:Q\to Q'$, compare $\beta_{P',Q'}F(H_A(a,b))$ and $H_B(Fa,Fb)\beta_{P,Q}$. Their transposes have domain $F H_A(P,Q)\otimes FP'$. Substitute the evaluation equation of step 3 into both. Naturality of $c$ and the naturality of the closed adjunction in its tensor parameter and target make each transpose equal to $F\bigl(b\,e^A_{P,Q}(1\otimes a)\bigr)c_{H_A(P,Q),P'}$. Injectivity of $\operatorname{tr}_B$ gives the desired equality, including the contravariant first variable.

source.place: Tags 08J9 and 07A4; direct naturality computation for evaluation mates.

proof.text: Let $t:X\otimes P\to Q$ be any derived morphism, and put $\widehat t=\operatorname{tr}_A(t)$. Then $\beta_{P,Q}F(\widehat t)=\operatorname{tr}_B(F(t)c_{X,P})$. Indeed, the inverse transpose of its left side is $F(e^A)c_{H_A(P,Q),P}(F\widehat t\otimes1)=F\bigl(e^A(\widehat t\otimes1)\bigr)c_{X,P}=F(t)c_{X,P}$, by naturality of $c$. The inverse transpose of its right side is the same morphism. This gives preservation of transposition for every parameter object $X$, without asserting that beta is invertible.

For $P,Q,T\in D(A)$ define internal composition $m_A:H_A(Q,T)\otimes H_A(P,Q)\to H_A(P,T)$ as the transpose of $e^A_{Q,T}(1\otimes e^A_{P,Q})\alpha$, where $\alpha:(H_A(Q,T)\otimes H_A(P,Q))\otimes P\to H_A(Q,T)\otimes(H_A(P,Q)\otimes P)$. Define $m_B$ in the same way. This is precisely internal composition for the fixed closed structure: it is determined by the equation $e^A_{P,T}(m_A\otimes1_P)=e^A_{Q,T}(1\otimes e^A_{P,Q})\alpha$, and similarly for $B$. The closed adjunction makes this a definition and the displayed equation its inverse-transpose formula.

source.place: Tag 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition) and Tag 08J9; composition as the transpose of iterated evaluation.

proof.text: Set $U=H_A(Q,T)$ and $V=H_A(P,Q)$. The composition identity is $\beta_{P,T}F(m_A)c_{U,V}=m_B(\beta_{Q,T}\otimes\beta_{P,Q})$. Untranspose both sides against $FP$. By step 3, the left side becomes $F(e^A_{P,T})c_{H_A(P,T),P}(F m_A\otimes1)(c_{U,V}\otimes1)$. Naturality of $c$, the equation of step 6, and the associativity equation of step 2 rewrite this as the following explicit composite: $F(e^A_{Q,T})c_{U,Q}(1_{FU}\otimes F(e^A_{P,Q}))(1_{FU}\otimes c_{V,P})\alpha_B$. For the right side, step 6 first gives $e^B_{FQ,FT}(\beta_{Q,T}\otimes(e^B_{FP,FQ}(\beta_{P,Q}\otimes1)))\alpha_B$. Substituting step 3 for each of the two evaluations gives exactly that same explicit composite. The two transposes are equal, hence the required composition identity follows by the closed bijection.

source.place: Tags 08J9 and 0A98; two substitutions of the defining evaluation equation, with canonical tensor associativity from step 2.

proof.text: For each site, use the uniquely specified composition map of actual signed Hom complexes, which has the component formula g tensor h maps to g composed with h. This directly gives the required composition representative formula after applying a component to a section. To construct evaluation, let O be the coefficient unit concentrated in degree zero. Assemble the specified unit-evaluation maps Hom(O,L)^n to L^n into a chain isomorphism u_L using their differential compatibility and degreewise invertibility. Its map on sections is projection to source degree zero followed by evaluation on the section corresponding to 1. Define evaluation as (identity tensor u_L inverse), then composition Hom(L,M) tensor Hom(O,L) to Hom(O,M), then u_M. Naturality of the sheaf tensor generator and its total-summand inclusion gives its action on a pure tensor. The composition formula makes this h applied to u_L(u_L inverse(x)) = h(x), proving the required evaluation formula without extra signs. All chain maps and signed differentials are those of the given tensor and Hom complexes.

source.place: Tags 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), 0A90 (lemma-compose), 08J9 and 0A98; expansion of the signed differentials on representative evaluation and composition.
